issues.failure_explanation: For n strictly inside a batch the proof asserts sigma_n(f_n) >= sigma_{ñ}(f_n) >= sigma_{ñ+1}(f_{ñ+1}). Neither inequality is supported: f_n lies in V_{n+1} ⊂ V_{ñ} for n<ñ, so sigma_{ñ}(f_n)=0, and there is no relation between dist(f_n,V_n) and the residual of the later greedy pick f_{ñ+1}. The claim itself is false: the non-leading elements are chosen by the surrogate at the batch start (or arbitrarily, per the remark) and their residual w.r.t. V_n can be arbitrarily small. Counterexample: X=R^3, b=2, gamma=1, F={e1, (e1+eps e2)/sqrt(1+eps^2), e3/2}. Line 3 picks f_0=e1, line 5 picks f_1=(e1+eps e2)/sqrt(1+eps^2), so |a_{1,1}|=eps/sqrt(1+eps^2), while sigma_{1+b-1}=sigma_2=1/2. The Banach lemma repeats the identical step. Since Theorem th:wbg_hilbert bounds prod|a_{n+i,n+i}| from below via (P1), and all rate results are derived from it, they fail too; e.g. F consisting of e^{-c_0 k}e_k plus, for each k, b-1 near-copies e^{-c_0 k}(e_k+eps phi_{k,j}) with fresh orthonormal phi_{k,j} has d_n ≤ e^{-c_0 n} but the batch greedy spends b-1 picks per batch on useless directions, giving sigma_{b l} ≈ e^{-c_0(l+1)}, i.e. sigma_n ≈ e^{-c_0 n/b}; with b=100, n=1000, c_0=0.01, alpha=1 this gives sigma_n≈0.896 while Theorem col:wbg_hilbert(iii) asserts sigma_n ≤ sqrt2 e^{-0.83}≈0.62, and (i) is violated similarly.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace (P1) by a bound that only uses the leading element of each batch (e.g. work with the subsequence of spaces V_{b l} and the greedy-chosen elements) and restate all rate theorems with a loss that depends on b (effectively rates in terms of n/b), abandoning the claimed b-independent constants and the (2/3)^alpha corollary.
issues.overall_effect: All convergence-rate results for the batch greedy (Hilbert and Banach case), the claimed b-independent asymptotic rate loss factor (2/3)^alpha, and the introductory/numerical-section claims that the asymptotic rate is preserved and that only minor modifications of the DeVore et al. proofs are needed, are unsupported and in general false for large b.
issues.title: Lower bound in (P1) is false for non-leading batch elements; core convergence results fail
issues.why_classification: The central theorems are false as stated (explicit counterexamples), and any correct version must materially worsen the advertised rate guarantees to a b-dependent loss, so the main mathematical contribution does not survive in comparable form.

issues.failure_explanation: In (ii) and (iii) the constants are defined with the ceiling factor evaluated at n (the index of sigma_n), but the proof derives inequalities with the factor evaluated at s, where M = ceil(4+(b-1)/s)s (resp. ceil(2+(b-1)/s)s), so s < M. Since ceil(4+(b-1)/n) is decreasing in n, C_1(M,b) can be strictly smaller than 2^{alpha+1}gamma^{-2}ceil(4+(b-1)/s)^{2alpha}C_0, so the derived inequality is consistent with the definition and no contradiction arises (e.g. b=10, s=1, M=13: definition uses 5^{2alpha}, proof needs 13^{2alpha}). Likewise in (iii), c_1(M,b) ≥ 2^{-1-alpha}ceil(2+(b-1)/s)^{-alpha}c_0 for M>s, so the claimed contradiction c_1 > that value is not one. In addition, the induction step in (ii) applies the hypothesis with C_1 at index 2s while the contradiction is sought against C_1 at index M, although C_1(·,b) varies with the index. Independently of ISSUE-001, the stated constants (and Remark Rem:c1's monotonicity claims, the second remark's thresholds n ≥ b+3 / n ≥ b+1, and Cor:expDecay's factor for n ≥ b) are therefore not proven; the same pattern appears in theo:Banach (ii),(iii).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the case analysis with a fixed constant per n-range: define the constants using the ceiling factor at s (i.e. at roughly n/4 or n/2, or use the worst case (3+b)^{2alpha}, (1+b)^{-alpha}), and adjust the thresholds in the remarks and Cor:expDecay accordingly (e.g. n ≳ 4b instead of n ≥ b+3).
issues.overall_effect: Even if the rate estimates were otherwise valid, the specific n- and b-dependence of the constants and the thresholds (n ≥ b-1, n ≥ b+1, n ≥ b+3) at which the b-independent constants 5^{2alpha}, 6^{-alpha} are claimed to hold are unsupported.
issues.title: n-dependent constants C_1(n,b), c_1(n,b) not established by the contradiction argument
issues.why_classification: A contained reworking of the constants and thresholds is needed; the form of the estimates is preserved but the announced regime in which b-independent constants hold shifts, so it is more than a local typo fix but no new architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: Case 3 of (ii) needs C_1 ≥ (4ceil(2+(b-1)/4)-1)^{alpha-beta-1/2}, but the second term of C_1(n,b) is 4(ceil(2+(b-1)/4)-1)^{alpha-beta-1/2}, which is smaller whenever p=alpha-beta-1/2 is not small: for b=1 it requires 4·7^{-p} ≥ 1, false for p > ln4/ln7 ≈ 0.71 (e.g. alpha=2, beta=0.1). In Case 2 of (iii) the chain uses sqrt(2g s)e^{-c_1(2g s)^alpha} ≤ sqrt(M)e^{-c_1 M^alpha} for M < 2gs (the stated inequality M ≥ 2gs is also reversed), which requires x ↦ sqrt(x)e^{-c_1 x^alpha} to be decreasing on [M,2gs]; this fails for small M when c_1 is small and is not justified.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the second term of C_1(n,b) by (4ceil(2+(b-1)/4)-1)^{alpha-beta-1/2}, and in (iii) Case 2 bound sqrt(M)e^{-c_1M^alpha} ≥ sqrt(g s)e^{-c_1(2gs)^alpha} and sigma_{gs} ≤ C_1 sqrt(gs) e^{-c_0 s^alpha/2} directly, which yields the same exponent comparison.
issues.overall_effect: The stated constant in theo:Banach (ii) is not valid for all admissible alpha, beta, and the Case 2 argument of (iii) has a gap; the rates themselves are unaffected once constants are adjusted.
issues.title: Banach-space corollary: Case 3 constant insufficient and unjustified monotonicity in Case 2 of (iii)
issues.why_classification: Both defects are fixed by local changes of a constant and a two-line re-arrangement of an inequality chain, preserving the stated rates.
